title: Deterministic Mocks at the AI Boundary — Check

questions.prompt: Why is the AI search implemented as a deterministic mock rather than a live LLM call in the core path?
questions.explanation: A deterministic stub yields the same output for the same input, so tests are repeatable, fast, network-free, and can assert exact results.
options: LLMs cannot be called from TypeScript
Determinism makes tests repeatable, offline, and exactly assertable
It is cheaper to write fewer tests
The frontend cannot parse LLM output

questions.prompt: Placing a non-deterministic LLM call inside the core compute path tends to make a test suite flaky and force loose assertions.
questions.explanation: Non-deterministic outputs vary run to run, so tests can only assert loosely and may fail intermittently regardless of code correctness.

questions.prompt: What design move keeps the rest of the system deterministic even if a real model is used later?
questions.explanation: An explicit seam lets the mock answer in tests/dev while a real model could sit behind the same boundary later, leaving the deterministic core untouched.
options: Hiding the AI behind an explicit, swappable seam at the boundary
Calling the model from every domain module
